svg.title: Expert-conditioned history retrieval: innovations 1, 2, and 3
svg.desc: Shared HSTU or SASRec history encoding prepares target-independent memory with item-expert-specific dictionaries. Each actual ad expert supplies its own query, active sparse-code atoms, and continuous coefficients. Two scoring paths combine direct attention over selected events and coefficient-weighted summaries of the remaining history. Expert scores are mixed after interaction.
svg.text: Ranking-style history interaction for retrieval
Prepare user memory once. Let each actual ad expert read detailed evidence and the compressed tail.
Actual-ad cross-attention
Read selected events with the actual candidate query.
Ad-derived codebook memory
Reusable selections and weighted tail summaries.
Item-expert-specific interaction
Multiple queries; a codebook system for each expert.
SHARED MODEL PARAMETERS
Expert-specific dictionaries C[e, atom] + learned atom-to-history queries a[e, atom]
Ad structure learned in parameters
No target-ad features enter user preparation
USER-ONLY PREPARATION
User history: event identities, actions, and timestamps
Only the valid causal prefix; independent of every candidate ad
One shared HSTU / SASRec history encoder
Preserve event-level keys and values K/V; share them across experts
Build a memory slot for every expert / dictionary atom
Latent relevance: w[t] = exp(a · k[t] / √d)
Code queries organize the history before a target ad is known
Selected raw events
Top-b indices for each slot
Keep original event K/V
Shared storage; lists reference events
Preserve position and action/time payloads
Full-history summaries
Z = Σ w[t]
U = Σ w[t] × v[t]
One scalar + one value vector per slot
Target-independent sums over valid history
Reusable memory for every candidate
ITEM-ONLY PREPARATION
Actual ad features → shared item feature encoder
Static-ad outputs can be cached for a fixed model and codebook version
Item experts: q₁, q₂, …, qE
Keep E distinct queries through interaction; do not average them first
Sparse ad-to-latent coding
Nonnegative codes; top-K active atoms
Active atoms address user-memory slots
Continuous ad gates
Normalize coefficients → weights α[e,j]
Item-only expert gates π[e] mix final scores
Prepared item state — independent of the user
For each expert e: query q[e] + active atom indices + sparse coefficients
Item-only gate π[e] combines expert scores after their interactions
Each item expert retains its own query, codebooks, and history reads
Active atoms select memory; coefficient magnitudes control the read
Cached item queries, codes, and gates
USER–ITEM SCORING — REPEAT THE TWO PATHS FOR EACH ITEM EXPERT
Read prepared memory and selected events; do not rescan omitted history for every ad.
Gather memory slots using expert e's active sparse-code atoms
Union and deduplicate selected event positions → S[e]; retain active summary statistics
PATH A · SELECTED RAW EVENTS
Actual query q[e] cross-attends directly to event K/V in S[e]
Normalize actual-ad attention over the deduplicated selected set
Output: r_raw[e]
Exact on retained events; not equivalent to full-history attention
PATH B · ACTIVATION-WEIGHTED TAIL SUMMARIES
For each active slot: subtract all S[e] event contributions from U and Z
Normalize each tail summary, then mix using this ad's weights α[e,j]
Output: r_tail[e] = Σ α[e,j] × z_tail[e,j]
No raw/tail overlap within an expert; handle empty tails with a mask
Expert score s[e] = G[e](q[e], r_raw[e], r_tail[e], masks)
One history interaction per expert; combine evidence before mixing experts
FINAL RETRIEVAL LOGIT: s(u, i) = Σ π[e](i) × s[e](u, i)
Exact chunked catalog scoring first · compare accuracy, memory, and compute
Design boundary
User-only memory + item-only queries/codes → candidate-specific reads in the scorer
Selected events retain detail; activation-weighted tail summaries retain broader user context.
